title: Posting run — the weekend's work, exposed in order
dates: prepared 2026-09-07 · for the working group call Tuesday 2026-09-08, 11:00 ET / 15:00 UTC
lead: Everything built between 5 and 7 September, in the order it should leave the machine. Each step names what it exposes, where it goes, which draft carries it, and what gates it. Steps are not independent: a later step reads wrong if an earlier one has not happened, and the order below is the only claim this page makes. Nothing here posts itself.

phases.title: Before anything leaves the machine
phases.why: Two sentences are missing from the draft and both are the author's to write. Neither is hard; both are visible on the rendered title page, which is why they come before the first commit rather than after it.

steps.act: Write the relicensing sentence into the specification's appendix
steps.gate: author's own words — no tool writes this
steps.why: The Cryptographic Background is adapted from the author's earlier expository work. The appendix must say so and state the licence under which it enters a ToIP deliverable. It is the sentence a Linux Foundation reviewer looks for first.

steps.act: Confirm the editors line with the chair
steps.where: spec/header.md — currently editor: Mitchell Travers; Scott Jones under contributors
steps.why: It appears on the rendered title page of a working group deliverable. Cheaper to agree before the commit than to amend after it.

steps.act: Run the checks one last time
steps.where: node board/test.mjs · node --test board/review.test.mjs · node tools/zkbook-export.mjs --check · cd ~/dtgwg-zkp-spec && npm run render && node conformance/test.mjs
steps.why: Run the current suites and regeneration checks. Passing results support the recorded scope of the tests; they do not certify cryptographic correctness or adoption.

phases.title: The specification repository — the pull request
phases.why: This is the single highest-value act of the run. It turns 'a draft is ready' into a link the task force can read, and every post in phase C is easier to write once it exists. Three commits, each readable alone, each carrying the rite footer above its sign-off.

steps.act: Commit C1 — front matter and repository description
steps.where: specs.json · README.md · spec/header.md · spec/intro.md · spec/terms-and-definitions-intro.md · spec/appendix.md · the two placeholder terms removed
steps.gate: push-rite serve → speak → footer, then git commit -s; no AI co-author trailer on upstream commits
steps.why: Readable alone: what the specification is, how it is produced, that generated sections carry a source digest.

steps.act: Commit C2 — the conformance apparatus and its CI
steps.where: conformance/records · requests · stacks · schema · validate.mjs · test.mjs · README.md · .github/workflows/validate-conformance.yml
steps.why: A reviewer who trusts nothing else can read this commit and run it. The validator's refusals are register strings; the test fails when generated text is stale.

steps.act: Commit C3 — the body and the generated terms
steps.gate: its own rite entry; DCO; the digest stamp must match C2's records
steps.why: Generated from C2. Reviewers who distrust generated prose read C3 against C2 and run the test rather than taking anyone's word.

steps.act: Push the branch and open the draft pull request
steps.why: Body P says what is generated and what is written, how to review each commit, and what the draft does not do: it selects no construction and claims no soundness.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Resolve phase A prerequisites, then open this as a draft PR.

phases.title: Expose the weekend's work — the posts, in order
phases.why: Four posts carry the whole weekend. The first is the anchor and the others read as its consequences; posted in any other order they read as four unrelated announcements. The last three are timed to the call: two of them are cross-task-force and land better before Tuesday than after it.

steps.act: Post the consolidated anchor — what the draft is, what kind of document it is, who wrote it, and the four review rounds
steps.why: One opening post in place of the two long forms. It proposes the review process, states the informative status and asks three questions. Add the actual draft-PR link before publishing; the group has not yet agreed the review schedule.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Open draft PR P; insert its actual URL and update the PR status sentences.

steps.act: Post the four work items with their record identifiers, plus Flock
steps.why: The chair takes the artifact gap to the paper's authors on Tuesday. His four items each having a record identifier changes what he can ask them. Before the call, not after.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Open draft PR P and publish consolidated anchor R; include their actual links.

steps.why: Filed 5 September; its third tracked item is coordination with this task force's Q2. That is record 008. It is also an agenda row, and answering beforehand means the row reports rather than promises.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Open draft PR P and publish consolidated anchor R; include their actual links.

steps.act: Place the seed set as record form
steps.why: The board thread has not seen the twelve records or the four proving systems. Can follow the call rather than precede it — it is a working-list update, not a decision.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Open draft PR P and publish consolidated anchor R; include their actual links.

phases.title: Prep for the working group call
phases.why: The chair drafted Tuesday's agenda on the wiki and left four questions addressed to the co-chair. Answering them in his draft rather than on the call is most of the preparation.

steps.act: Send the agenda proposal to the chair
steps.where: calls/2026-09-08/AGENDA-PROPOSED.md — his four bracketed questions answered, a nine-row table, a replacement reference list, five decisions and seven action items
steps.gate: none — it is a proposal, and the agenda is his
steps.why: Two new rows (where the work lands · blinded binders) and a stated fallback that collapses them into one eight-minute item if the Berkeley conversation runs long.

steps.act: Update the meeting-notes page, if he wants it done directly
steps.gate: CONFLUENCE_EMAIL + CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN in the shell; CONFLUENCE_EXPECT_VERSION=2
steps.why: The whole body, built by editing the pulled page rather than rewriting it. Three things change someone else's draft — read the directory's README before pushing.

phases.title: Side notes — disclosed, not proposed
phases.why: Two projects of the author's own touch this work. Both are named on the record so that neither surfaces later as a surprise, and neither asks for anything to be adopted.

steps.act: Disclose the agent-first verifiable trust agent implementation as a testbed
steps.where: trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf — a comment on pull request #21, or a short reply under the anchor
steps.why: Record 020 and the agent-runtimes document describe an agent acting for a member within a scope, and neither has an implementation to fail against. This is an attempt at one, inverted: the agent is the member being admitted rather than an accessory to a human who is really the member. Post last, and after the pull request is open, so it reads as a footnote to the delegation lane rather than as a pitch.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Open draft PR P and publish consolidated anchor R; include their actual links.

steps.act: The credentials-side long form, if a thread asks for it
steps.gate: proverb unserved — serve one at posting time
steps.why: The same project read against the credential vocabulary, with five questions about issuance, lapsing roles and what counts as edge evidence. Do not post it in the same week as the side note above; one disclosure at a time.
requires: Re-read the live destination and resolve changes since the source snapshot.
Held: only prepare for publication if a relevant thread requests it.

afterwards: F (cred-spec #9, the common-control linkage) and J (cred-spec #31, the merge plan pointer) — both fine after the call.
L (zkp-tf #17, the SIROS catalog as an as-signed proving-system entry) — pairs with whatever the call decides about construction selection.
I (cred-spec PR #26 carve-out) is optional; D (the board-item detail thread) waits for a Projects board that does not exist yet.

Re-read card 020's issuance clauses against the merged delegation credential text (door D17), and measure what the records currently call conjecture: construction 001 over a BLAKE3 tree, construction 007's compile.
